sq.q: Why does Best Fit sometimes result in more fragmentation than First Fit?
answer: Best Fit tries to minimize leftover space by choosing the smallest possible block, but this often leaves many small, unusable holes in memory, increasing external fragmentation . First Fit may leave larger but more usable fragments.

lq.q: Explain Contiguous Memory Allocation and its strategies. Compare the advantages and disadvantages of each strategy.
answer: Contiguous memory allocation is one of the earliest memory management schemes used in operating systems. It involves allocating a single contiguous block of physical memory to each process. (20%) The Operating System (OS) maintains a free memory list , and allocation is done based on certain strategies.
When a process arrives, the OS selects a free block large enough to accommodate it, using one of the following strategies:
Allocates the first available block that is large enough.
Allocates the first available block that is large enough.
It scans memory from the beginning and assigns the first matching hole .
It scans memory from the beginning and assigns the first matching hole .
Advantage: Fast; low overhead
Advantage: Fast; low overhead
Disadvantage: Can lead to many small unused holes (external fragmentation)
Disadvantage: Can lead to many small unused holes (external fragmentation)
Allocates the smallest hole that is big enough.
Allocates the smallest hole that is big enough.
It searches the entire list and selects the best match .
It searches the entire list and selects the best match .
Advantage: Minimizes wasted space
Advantage: Minimizes wasted space
Disadvantage: Slower due to full search; may leave tiny unusable fragments
Disadvantage: Slower due to full search; may leave tiny unusable fragments
Allocates the largest available hole .
Allocates the largest available hole .
Idea is to leave large blocks behind for future use.
Idea is to leave large blocks behind for future use.
Advantage: May avoid many small holes
Advantage: May avoid many small holes
Disadvantage: Often leads to inefficient space usage
